GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Past tense of a verb + ことがある says you have had the experience at least once.
GrammarPatterns.Examples:
日本に行ったことがあります。 = I have been to Japan.
寿司を食べたことがない。 = I have never eaten sushi.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Using the dictionary form (行くことがある) means “sometimes go”.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: After nouns or て-form: only/always. After た-form: just finished.
GrammarPatterns.Examples:
彼は文句ばかり言う。 = He does nothing but complain.
今起きたばかりです。 = I just woke up.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Confusing たばかり (subjective “just”) with たところ (exact timing).

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Verb dictionary/ない form + ようにする: try to make something a habit.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: 毎日運動するようにしています。 = I try to exercise every day.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Using ようになる (change of state) when you mean an effort.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Softly denies a conclusion the listener might draw.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: 嫌いなわけではない。 = It's not that I dislike it.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Positive cause. Use せいで for a negative cause.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: 先生のおかげで合格しました。 = I passed thanks to my teacher.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Using おかげで for bad results — use せいで instead.

GrammarPatterns.Pattern: If + S + had + V3, S + would have + V3
GrammarPatterns.Meaning: Imagined past result that did not happen
GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Third conditional. The if-clause can come first or second; use a comma only when it comes first.
GrammarPatterns.Examples:
If I had studied, I would have passed. = I didn't study, so I failed.
She would have come if you had asked. = You didn't ask, so she didn't come.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: “If I would have known…” — never use would in the if-clause.

GrammarPatterns.Pattern: S + would rather + V + than + V
GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Both verbs are bare infinitives. Short form: 'd rather.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: I would rather stay home than go out tonight. = I prefer staying home.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Wrong: I would rather to stay. Right: I would rather stay.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: When Not only starts the sentence, invert subject and auxiliary.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: Not only is it cheap, but it is also fast. = It is cheap and fast.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Forgetting inversion: “Not only it is cheap…”.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Useful in academic writing to present common views.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: It is widely believed that cars should be banned from city centres. = Many people think so.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Followed by a noun or gerund, not a clause.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: Despite the rain, we went out. = Even though it rained, we went out.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: “Despite it rained” — use although for a clause.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Attach to a verb stem to talk about plans or guesses.
GrammarPatterns.Examples:
내일 도서관에 갈 거예요. = I'm going to the library tomorrow.
비가 올 거예요. = It will probably rain.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Dropping 으 after a consonant stem: 먹을 거예요, not 먹ㄹ 거예요.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Verb stem + 고 싶다 for the speaker's wishes.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: 한국에 가고 싶어요. = I want to go to Korea.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Using 싶다 for a third person — use 고 싶어하다.

GrammarPatterns.Explanation: Connects reason or sequence; cannot be used with imperatives.
GrammarPatterns.Examples: 배가 고파서 밥을 먹었어요. = I was hungry, so I ate.
GrammarPatterns.CommonMistakes: Using 아서 with commands: use (으)니까 instead.

WritingPrompts.Title: Should cities ban cars?
WritingPrompts.PromptText: Some people think private cars should be banned from city centres. Do you agree or disagree? Give reasons and examples.

WritingPrompts.Title: Technology and loneliness
WritingPrompts.PromptText: Does technology make people more or less lonely? Discuss both views and give your opinion.

WritingPrompts.Title: Describe your ideal study space
WritingPrompts.PromptText: Where do you focus best? Describe the place, the time of day and why it works for you.

WritingPrompts.Title: 週末の予定
WritingPrompts.PromptText: 今週末の予定について書いてください。誰と、どこで、何をしますか。

WritingPrompts.Title: 私の苦手なこと
WritingPrompts.PromptText: 苦手なことについて書いてください。どうやって克服していますか。

WritingPrompts.Title: 나의 하루
WritingPrompts.PromptText: 오늘 하루에 대해 써 보세요. 무엇을 했어요? 기분이 어땠어요?

WritingPieces.Title: Should cities ban cars?
WritingPieces.Content:
Many large cities are struggling with congestion and poor air quality. Banning private cars from the centre is one radical answer, and I believe it is worth trying.

First, fewer cars would mean lower emissions. Children walking to school would breathe cleaner air, and streets could be redesigned for every pedestrian rather than for traffic.

However, a ban only works if people have another way to commute. Cities would need to invest in infrastructure such as frequent buses and safe cycle lanes before cars disappear.

In conclusion, a car-free centre is a good idea, but only as part of a wider plan.

WritingPieces.Title: My favourite place to study
WritingPieces.Content: My favourite place to study is a small library near my home. It is quiet in the morning and the desks face a large window, so I can concentrate for hours. I usually arrive at eight, put my phone in my bag and start with vocabulary review. The routine helps me stay focused and makes studying feel less like a chore.

WritingPieces.Title: Technology and loneliness
WritingPieces.Content: Smartphones are ubiquitous, yet many people say they feel lonely. Some argue that social media connects us, while others believe it replaces real conversations. In my view, technology is not detrimental in itself; the problem is how we use it.

WritingPieces.Title: 週末の予定について
WritingPieces.Content: 今週末は友達と京都に行く予定です。朝早く起きて、電車で行きます。お寺を見たり、抹茶を飲んだりしたいです。準備はもうできました。

WritingPieces.Title: 私の苦手なこと
WritingPieces.Content: 私は人前で話すのが苦手です。でも、毎日少しずつ練習するようにしています。

WritingPieces.Title: 나의 하루
WritingPieces.Content: 아침에 친구를 만났어요. 같이 도서관에서 공부했어요. 내일도 갈 거예요.

WritingPieces.Title: A city I would like to visit
WritingPieces.Content: I would like to visit Kyoto because of its temples and quiet streets. I have never been to Japan, but my friends say the autumn colours are beautiful.
